content.text:
The hypothesis doesn't hold: no sizeable customer, part family or order-size group consistently loses money once material and labour are charged. I've saved the finding (F4) with no dollar figure, because there's no loss big enough to size. My working notes are saved as `notes.md`.

To test it, I charged each job its material purchase orders, plus its clocked hours at that year's full shop cost per hour. That rate is direct and indirect labour, benefits and overhead from the general ledger divided by clocked hours. It rose from $102.8/h in 2016 to $150.9/h in 2025 (q106).

- **Customers:** the 51 customers with at least $500k of revenue bring in 88.8% of it. They all earn $139.9–$236.0 per clocked hour after material, above the 10-year cost of $124.9/h (q113). Only 6 of 296 customer-years with $100k+ of revenue fall below that year's cost, and 4 of those are in 2021. No customer is below it in two different years (q137).
- **Part families and order sizes:** there is a clear gap but no loss. Jobs of 1–5 pieces earn $142.0/h against $206.9/h for jobs over 100 pieces, and family 6 earns $142.0/h against $200.5/h for family 1. All of these are above the shop's cost (q118).
- **The thin edge:** family 6 jobs of 1–5 pieces cover cost in 9 of 10 years, but only just. In 2020 they made $128.1/h against a cost of $126.2/h (q130).
- **2021:** this was the only broad dip; the plant's operating margin fell to 5.36% that year. Five family/order-size groups with $2.10M of revenue fell short of cost by $122.6k in total (q122, q127). Material cost across the plant explains the year better than any hidden group of customers.
- **Parts that keep losing:** 22 of 1,151 repeat parts lose money over their life. Together that's –$83k across ten years, about $8.3k a year. Most are family 3 parts ordered around 6 at a time (q141, q145, q150).

**Limits:**
- Outside processing and premium freight appear only as ledger totals, so they aren't charged to jobs.
- Material is counted when ordered, including the 28.9% of purchase orders that never show a receipt.
- One plant-wide hourly cost hides differences between work centres.
- Single-job figures are noisy because labour entries are posting records of up to 208 hours. About 10,557 jobs come out negative, but this mostly evens out at part and customer level, so it isn't evidence of real losses.

**Suggested next step:** each year, check jobs of 5 pieces or fewer in families 3 and 6 against the shop's cost per hour. If the margin narrows further, test a minimum or setup charge on quotes, and review the 22 losing parts when they next come up for requote.
